_doc: The weekly scout report: what exists out there that this box is not using. Written by the Claude routine described in docs/models.md and read by src/lib/model-scout.ts. Judgment lives here; facts about which model ids a vendor currently sells are NOT — those are pulled live from each vendor's model-list endpoint at read time, because a list committed to git is out of date the day after it is written. Fit verdicts are likewise computed at read time and never stored here: a verdict depends on what is running and how much disk is free, and both change hourly. They are now computed PER HOST — measured against the machine this console is running on, and against each other host's declared specs in config/hosts/*.json — so a claim in `why` or `notes` that a model does not fit needs to name which machine it means.
_schema: candidates[]: { id, name, kind: local|cloud, capability, why, checkpoint?, provider?, target?, mode?, params?, released?, license?, docs?, paper?, requirement? { vramGb, ramGb, diskGb, basis, estimated }, spec? { paramsB, precision, contextK, kind }, runtimes?, pricing? }. Give `requirement` when the authors published usable numbers; give `spec` otherwise and let estimateFromParams() do the arithmetic with an honest basis string. `runtimes` pins weights to one stack (e.g. ["metal"] for an MLX repo) and MUST be omitted for portable weights, which is most of them — absent means "runs anywhere", and GGUF counts as portable. Verdicts are computed per HOST: name which machine you mean in `why` and `notes`, because BeTenshi (31.8 GB VRAM + 63 GB host RAM) and B5 (one 128 GB unified pool) disagree about a good number of models. upgrades[]: { alias, from, to, why } — a like-for-like repoint of an alias already in ai-router.yaml.

ON CV3-EVAL ENGLISH IN CLONING MODE, Audio8 is 1.17 WER / 11.29 RTFx / 59.16 SIM / UTMOS 4.00 against Chatterbox's 3.42 / 0.99 / 53.13 / no UTMOS score: 66% lower word error, 6.03 more speaker-similarity points, and ELEVEN TIMES the throughput. On the nine-language CV3 cloning view, where both have 9/9 coverage, it is 3.74 / 68.16 SIM against 6.11 / 66.40, and it is better in EVERY ONE of the nine languages (en 1.17 vs 3.42, zh 1.33 vs 4.90, fr 4.25 vs 8.85, es 2.61 vs 3.63, de 2.56 vs 4.12, it 3.47 vs 4.42, ja 6.68 vs 7.97, ko 5.19 vs 7.70, ru 6.41 vs 9.96). SAME LANGUAGE COUNT, SAME LICENCE CLASS, SMALLER: 23 declared languages against Chatterbox's 23, apache-2.0 against MIT, 2.57 GB against 23.65 GB on disk and 2.95 GB resident against 3.0 GB measured. AND THE INCUMBENT IS PARTLY BROKEN ON THIS BOX, which no earlier report in this file has mentioned and which is recorded in the repository itself: config/hosts/betenshi.json's runtimes block says 'local-chatterbox (the `voice` service) returns HTTP 500 for its own built-in voice; Kokoro synthesizes fine at the same endpoint, so Kokoro is the declared driver'. So BeTenshi's declared tts driver is Kokoro, and the cloning service it installed on 18-09 is not serving its own voice. ARABIC IS THE DECIDER AMONG CLEAN LICENCES. The card lists Arabic explicitly among the twelve languages Realistic-Air adds to Preview's eleven, and this box has an Arabic evaluation harness (config/arabic-eval.json, docs/arabic-model-experiment-2026-09-14.md). Of the clean-licensed cloners the board measures, Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base covers 10 languages and its own card names them — Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Russian, Portuguese, Spanish, Italian — with NO Arabic; VoxCPM2 declares 30 and OpenMOSS MOSS-TTS 20. Neither board measures Arabic at all, so this is a declared-coverage argument and not a measured one, and it is stated as such. WHERE IT LOSES, AND THESE MATTER. (1) It does NOT replace Kokoro on :8002: on CV3-Eval English reading it is 1.06 against Kokoro's 1.10, which is inside what a board rebuild moves, while Kokoro is 68.03 RTFx against 10.87 and UTMOS 4.51 against 4.43 at a thirtieth of the size. Kokoro stays the English reading default. (2) On English cloning SIM it is 13.51 points below tencent/AuK-Flash (59.16 vs 72.67), so if matching a reference speaker's identity matters more than intelligibility, the entry below is the one to take. (3) On nine-language reading it is 3.84 against Qwen3-TTS-CustomVoice's 3.64, and its Japanese is materially worse (8.68 against 5.90) — see notes for why that dropped the Qwen3-TTS candidate anyway. (4) UTMOS 4.00 in cloning mode is mid-table and Chatterbox has no UTMOS score, so as with AuK-Flash the board cannot say which SOUNDS better; listen before committing the service. THIS IS A BETENSHI ENTRY. The card's install line is 'Python 3.10 or newer and a CUDA-capable GPU are recommended' and its own device selection is `cuda if torch.cuda.is_available() else cpu` — there is no published Metal path, so on B5 the 128 GB pool is irrelevant and the fallback is CPU; whether torch MPS works through the custom remote code is untested and is NOT claimed here. That is the Iris-3B shape again, and NO `runtimes` PIN IS SET for the same reason: the weights are plain safetensors plus a .pth codec, both portable formats, and docs/models.md says the field speaks only where the FORMAT pins the hardware. Worth one line for B5 all the same: B5's declared tts is qwen3-tts-1.7b-customvoice, a speaker bank, so B5 has NO voice cloning at all — this would be an added capability there rather than a replacement, if a Metal path ever appears. ADOPTION, by metric per docs/models.md: 15,319 downloads in the last 30 days, which is also its all-time figure because the repo is 26 days old, and 367 likes. The 02-11 report said this model 'shipped 01-11 and is not on the board at all'; it is on the board now, which is the whole of what changed. Disk is EXACT from repo listings re-read 09-11 and byte-for-byte unchanged: vantagewithai/LongCat-Video-Avatar-1.5-GGUF-ComfyUI LongCat-Avatar-15_comfy-Q4_K_S.gguf 11,665,875,968 B + this repo's whisper-large-v3/model.safetensors 3,087,130,976 B + vocal_separator/Kim_Vocal_2.onnx 66,759,214 B + meituan-longcat/LongCat-Video vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors 507,591,892 B = 15,327,358,050 B. DOWNLOAD WITH AN --include LIST OR THIS COSTS FOUR TIMES WHAT IT SHOULD, which is new this week and is a file-listing finding rather than a model one: the whisper-large-v3/ subfolder alone ships FOUR redundant copies of the same weights — model.safetensors 3.09 GB, model.fp32 shards 6.17 GB, flax_model.msgpack 6.17 GB and pytorch_model.bin plus its fp32 pair 9.26 GB — about 24.7 GB for a 3.09 GB model, and the avatar repo as a whole is 56.36 GB on main (74.88 GB by usedStorage) because it carries bf16 shards, an int8 quantisation and a 2.52 GB DMD LoRA beside them. ONE REUSE IS ASSUMED AND MUST BE CHECKED BEFORE IT IS COUNTED AS FREE: the text encoder is google/umt5-xxl (confirmed from LongCat-Video/text_encoder/config.json, UMT5EncoderModel, 22.72 GB at fp32), which is the same encoder Wan 2.2 loads, and config/model-meta.json's basis for local-wan2.2-14b records 'the 6.7 GB text encoder' — the fp8-scaled UMT5-XXL ComfyUI uses. So the encoder is very probably already on the weights drive and is excluded from diskGb; if it is not, add about 6.7 GB. VRAM 13.4 is the Q4_K_S DiT x 1.15 and is a WORKING-MINIMUM ADMISSION FIGURE in the same sense model-meta uses for every video alias on this box, NOT an empty-card peak — the 02-10 bake-off measured whole-card peaks of 28.0-30.1 GB for the three installed video models whose admission figures are 14-16 GB, so expect the same shape here. RAM 26 covers the 6.7 GB encoder, 3.09 GB Whisper, 0.51 GB VAE and ComfyUI's own working set with the same headroom model-meta gives local-hunyuanvideo-1.5 (24 GB). NOTHING HERE IS MEASURED ON EITHER BOX. For reference, the authors' own route is far more expensive: bf16 DiT 31.71 + dmd_lora 2.52 + whisper 3.09 + vocal separator 0.07 + fp32 UMT5-XXL 22.72 + VAE 0.51 = 60.62 GB, or 44.79 GB using the repo's own base_model_int8 (15.88 GB).

candidates.why: STILL THE ONLY CANDIDATE THE `avatar` LANE HAS, AND THE LANE WAS RE-SWEPT THIS WEEK RATHER THAN ASSUMED: searching the hub for avatar, talking heads and lip-sync on 09-11 returns this repo at the top of trending, and the only other audio-driven options are Quark-Vision/Live-Avatar (apache-2.0 over Wan2.2-S2V-14B, 265 likes but ZERO downloads on both metrics and nearly a year old) and cicada-ai/Chanjing-Avatar-V2V-1.3B (apache-2.0, 2,906 downloads, 1 like) — neither publishes a comparison with anything, so on adoption and licence, which is what docs/models.md says this lane ranks on, this is still the entry. First raised 2026-11-02 on the branch that never merged. WHAT IT WOULD LET THE OWNER MAKE THAT NEITHER BOX CAN MAKE TODAY, which is the bar docs/models.md sets for an empty lane: a character who speaks. Both boxes can write a script, read it aloud (Chatterbox or Kokoro on BeTenshi, Qwen3-TTS on B5) and animate a still forward (Wan/LTX/Hunyuan in ComfyUI), and nothing joins those three — there is no path from an audio clip to a face whose mouth matches it. This model takes audio plus a still plus a prompt (AT2V, ATI2V and video continuation, single- or multi-stream audio) and holds identity across a long clip. AND IT LANDS ON A KNOWN PROBLEM RATHER THAN A HYPOTHETICAL ONE: docs/video-forge.md spends a whole section on continuity — characters redrawn from text every shot, a continuity-supervisor pass, first-frame cast checks, clips remade when they 'grow a person' — and the stated fix was character sheets plus hosted first frames. Audio-driven continuation with 'strict identity consistency' is the same problem attacked from the other end. WHY IT IS CHEAP HERE SPECIFICALLY: two of its three components are already on BeTenshi in some form. The audio encoder is Whisper-Large (the card says it replaced Wav2Vec2 with Whisper-Large for smoother lip dynamics) and the text encoder is UMT5-XXL, which is Wan 2.2's encoder — so the marginal download is the 11.67 GB Q4_K_S DiT plus a 3.09 GB HF Whisper checkpoint (BeTenshi's :8001 whisper is a CTranslate2 int8_float16 build at a self-reported 1.5 GB, so that one does NOT substitute) plus a 0.51 GB VAE. 15.33 GB for a capability, against the 20.3 GB the image service already costs. LICENCE IS CLEAN ON ALL THREE REPOS and that is rare in this lane: mit, not gated, on the avatar weights, on the LongCat-Video foundation repo its VAE and encoder come from, and on the GGUF repack. THIS IS A BETENSHI ENTRY. The authors' install needs torch cu124 and flash_attn 2.7.4.post1, which is CUDA, and B5 runs Draw Things rather than ComfyUI so the WanVideoWrapper route is not there either. NO `runtimes` PIN IS SET, deliberately and for the same reason as Audio8 above: GGUF and safetensors are portable formats and docs/models.md says runtimes must speak only where the FORMAT pins the hardware. ADOPTION, by metric: 3,804 downloads in the last 30 days and 13,935 all-time on the weights (3,391 / 12,911 a week ago); the GGUF repack is 24,270 and 94,466 (25,257 / 90,600), so the ComfyUI route is still where the users are and both are growing. WHAT IS NOT KNOWN, unchanged: nothing measures this. There is no avatar board, the only evaluation is the authors' own — 508 image-audio pairs, 770 crowdsourced raters, 13,240 judgements, 10 expert assessors over physical rationality, audio-visual harmony, temporal stability and identity consistency — reported as two figures in a PNG rather than as numbers, and benchmarked against unnamed 'leading commercial models'. So the ranking here is licence and adoption, per docs/models.md clause 5b, and no quality claim is made.
